note: Every legal statement the app makes is a row in this file. Nothing in the code is allowed to assert a rule that is not listed here, and nothing is shown without its status and source. Re-check the 'expected' rows before each document run: the statutory instruments behind them were not made when this file was last reviewed.

provisions.statement: A service charge is only payable to the extent that the costs were reasonably incurred, and any works were done to a reasonable standard.

A written demand for service charge must state the landlord's name and address. If that address is not in England or Wales, an address in England or Wales for the service of notices must also be given.
provisions.source: Landlord and Tenant Act 1987, sections 47 and 48
provisions.note: Until this information is given, the service charge is treated as not being due.

provisions.statement: A service charge demand must be accompanied by a summary of the leaseholder's rights and obligations, in the form set out in regulations. A leaseholder may withhold payment until it is provided.
provisions.source: Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, section 21B; Service Charges (Summary of Rights and Obligations, and Transitional Provision) (England) Regulations 2007 (SI 2007/1257)
provisions.note: This is one of the few service charge formats that IS prescribed today. The Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 is expected to replace it.

provisions.statement: A cost incurred more than 18 months before the demand is not recoverable, unless the leaseholder was told in writing within those 18 months that the cost had been incurred and would be charged to them.

Leaseholders must be consulted before qualifying works where any one leaseholder's share would be more than £250, and before a long-term agreement where any one leaseholder's share would be more than £100 a year. Without consultation, recovery is capped at those figures unless the tribunal grants dispensation.
provisions.source: Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, section 20; Service Charges (Consultation Requirements) (England) Regulations 2003 (SI 2003/1987)

provisions.statement: Service charge money paid by leaseholders is held on trust for them. It is not the company's money.
A leaseholder may ask in writing for a summary of the costs making up the service charge, and may then inspect the receipts and accounts behind it.
provisions.source: Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, sections 21 and 22
provisions.note: The Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 is expected to replace this request-led right with an annual report given to every leaseholder as a matter of course.

provisions.statement: The Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 received Royal Assent on 24 May 2024.
provisions.note: Royal Assent is not commencement. The service charge measures below need regulations before they do anything.

provisions.statement: The service charge measures in the Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 are expected to be brought in by statutory instrument. No date for them is settled.
provisions.source: Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 (c. 22), commencement provisions
provisions.note: Check the commencement regulations on legislation.gov.uk and the department's announcements before telling anybody a date.

provisions.statement: Service charge demands are expected to have to be made in a standardised form, carrying prescribed information.
provisions.source: Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 (c. 22), service charge provisions; form to be prescribed by regulations
provisions.note: The form has not been published. The demand template in this app is a working layout that carries the information a demand needs today, and is expected to need replacing wholesale once the form appears.

provisions.statement: A formal annual report is expected to have to be given to every leaseholder for each building, within a period and in a form to be set by regulations.
provisions.source: Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 (c. 22), service charge provisions; form and timing to be prescribed by regulations
provisions.note: Neither the contents nor the deadline are settled. Do not print a deadline for this.

provisions.statement: Service charge accounts are expected to have to follow a standardised form, and to be reported on by an accountant.
provisions.source: Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 (c. 22), service charge provisions; form to be prescribed by regulations

provisions.statement: Prescribed information about the building's insurance, including any commission paid, is expected to have to be given to leaseholders.
provisions.source: Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 (c. 22), insurance provisions; information to be prescribed by regulations

provisions.statement: The Energy Act 2023 makes provision for the regulation of heat networks in Great Britain, with Ofgem as the regulator.
provisions.source: Energy Act 2023, heat networks regulation provisions
provisions.note: The Act is the frame. The detail is in regulations and in Ofgem's authorisation conditions.

provisions.statement: Regulation of heat networks by Ofgem is expected to begin on 27 January 2026.
provisions.note: Taken from the project brief and NOT yet confirmed against Ofgem's published material. Confirm this date before it is put in front of a client.

provisions.statement: Heat network operators and suppliers are expected to have to register with Ofgem by 26 January 2027.
provisions.note: Taken from the project brief and NOT yet confirmed. This date drives the countdown on the front page - check it, and correct it here if it has moved.

provisions.statement: Operating a heat network without authorisation after the registration deadline is expected to be a criminal offence.
provisions.source: Energy Act 2023 and heat networks regulations
provisions.note: This is the reason the heat network side of this app exists. It is also the single statement most worth checking before repeating.

provisions.statement: Where a block of flats has communal heating, the party operating the network is often the resident management company, the RTM company, or its managing agent, rather than an energy business.
provisions.note: Who counts as the operator, and who as the supplier, is a question about your contracts and your lease. This app can only show you the question.

provisions.statement: Registered operators and suppliers are expected to be subject to ongoing authorisation conditions, covering matters such as pricing transparency, customer information, complaints handling and reporting.
provisions.note: The condition set in this app is a working list. Replace it with Ofgem's published conditions when they are final.
